newsitem.title: UK: Clarke raises personal allowances on income tax.
newsitem.headline: Clarke raises personal allowances on income tax.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he was raising the personal allowance on income on which no tax is paid and increasing the upper income tax threshold by 600 stg.
In his annual speech to parliament on the 1997/8 budget, he also said he was raising the 20 percent income tax band threshold by 200 stg from 3,900 stg.
"In this budget I am making an increase in the basic personal allowance of 280 stg," he said.
The tax-free allowance was raised by 240 stg to 3,765 stg in the last budget.
"I also propose to raise the threshold above which people start to pay the 40 percent higher tax rate by 600 stg," he said.
"As a further step towards that, I propose to widen the lower rate band of 20 percent tax by 200 stg, twice as much as required by indexation," Clarke said.
